2010_007_071310regmtg.paragraph: Agenda and board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, July 13, 2010 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. It carries minutes of the June 1, June 8 and June 15, 2010 sessions together with four competitive bid awards, an MHSAA membership resolution, a Section 105c Schools of Choice resolution, a Wattles sidewalk easement report, and the semiannual treasurer, depository and summer-tax resolutions. The largest purchase is elementary science kits from Delta Education at $138,280.00 charged to the 2004 Capital Projects Fund.
2010_007_071310regmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, Tuesday, July 13, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., except July and August.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the June 1, 2010 meeting, the June 8, 2010 workshop and the June 15, 2010 meeting, plus the copy paper bid award.

**Bid awards**

| Item | Bid | Vendor | Amount | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Copy paper | 9679 | Midland Paper | $44,288.16 | 2010-11 General Fund |
| Elementary science kits | 9683 | Delta Education | $138,280.00 | 2004 Capital Projects Fund |
| Playground surface materials | 9681 | Rolar Property Services | $74,340.00 | 2004 Capital Projects Fund |
| RF microphone equipment | 9684 | Videotape Products, Inc. | $24,623.05 | 2004 Capital Projects Fund |

Copy paper covers 1,680 cases of 8 1/2 x 11, 20#, 92-brightness paper at a unit price of 26.362; 13 of ten invited firms responded, one a No Bid. Science kits serve all 12 elementary schools, drawing four responses from 13 invitations, three of them No Bids. Playground surfacing replenishes safety surface at all 12 elementary schools, with one response from ten invitations. The microphone replacement is forced by FCC action barring frequencies long in public use; bid 9684 drew 21 valid responses plus one rejected fax. All four recommendations came from Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget, to Mark S. Rajter.

**Curriculum**
MHSAA membership for the six secondary schools from August 1, 2010 through July 31, 2011. A Schools of Choice resolution under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, for nonresident grade 10 students entering the International Academy East from districts in counties contiguous with the Oakland ISD; applications July 19 to August 3, 2010.

**Other business**
Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, is named Director and Patricia Orczykowski Alternate Director to the MAISL Joint Risk Management Trust, the district's property, casualty and liability carrier. Rajter reports on a proposed sidewalk easement at 553 Colebrook granted by Satyendra N. Basu for $1.00 to serve children walking to Wattles Elementary; no action required. Rajter is also appointed Board Treasurer for July through December 2010 under a depositories resolution naming Bank of America, Bank of New York, Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, MILAF and PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank. The Board is asked to continue summer collection of one-half of school property taxes for 2011-2012, to schedule a facilities-review workshop for Tuesday, August 17, 2010 at 5:30 p.m., and to close the meeting for negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

**From the June 15, 2010 minutes**
The 2009-10 budget amendment set the General Fund at $138,643,792, Special Revenue Funds at 7,682,186, Debt Service Funds at 18,461,564, Capital Project Funds at 3,288,459 and Internal Service Funds at 720,000. The 2010-2011 appropriations resolution set the General Fund at $135,793,505, Special Revenue Funds at 5,445,677, Debt Service funds at 18,590,065, Capital Project Funds at 7,216,120 and Internal Service Funds at 120,000, with millage of 18.0000 non-homestead general operating, 5.0381 homestead general operating, 4.7000 debt retirement on all properties and 11.0381 commercial personal property general operating. Contracts were extended for the Superintendent through June 30, 2013 and for assistant superintendents Richard M. Machesky and Jasen M. Witt through June 30, 2012. Jeremey Whan was appointed Principal of Bemis Elementary and Mark Rajter Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, both effective July 1, 2010. Retirees honored represented 1,046 years of service.
2010_007_071310regmtg.verbose:
**Meeting and agenda.** Board agenda and supporting packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, July 13, 2010, 7:00 PM, at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices are at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., except in July and August. The consent agenda comprises minutes of the June 1, 2010 meeting, the June 8, 2010 workshop and the June 15, 2010 meeting, plus the copy paper bid award.

**June 1, 2010 minutes (Athens High School).** President Underwood convened at 7:00 p.m. with members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Pochodylo; Superintendent Fowler; administrators Adamczyk, Davisson, Machesky, McAvoy and Witt; and approximately 600 staff, students and community members. Resolution 10-056 (Edmunds/Fleming) commended the music education staff after the NAMM Foundation named Troy one of the best communities for music education in America, citing fine arts coordinator P. Jefferson McCoy. An extended recognition block followed for middle school orchestras, the Athens High School Marching Band at the Bands of America Grand National championship in Indianapolis, Troy High bands that won seven awards at the National Heritage Music Festival in Boston on April 23 and 24, 13 Michigan Green Schools, fourteen middle schoolers with perfect Explore scores of 25, three high schoolers with perfect ACT scores of 36, and 42 National Merit semifinalists. Resolution 10-057 (Miletti/Philippart) renewed the food service management contract with Sodexo Management, Inc. for 2010/2011. Resolution 10-058 (Philippart/Fleming), under Public Act 419 of 2004 and following the May 18, 2010 open meeting, designated Mr. Todd Miletti the district's representative to the 2010 Oakland Schools Intermediate School District electoral body and directed him to vote at least on the first ballot at the June 7 election for Mrs. Barbara DeMarco and Mr. Connie R. Williams, CPA, FHFMA, each for six-year terms ending June 30, 2016, and Dr. Theresa Rich for a partial two-year term ending June 30, 2012; all three were unopposed. A negotiations closed session under Public Act 267, Section 8(c) carried 7-0; the Board closed at 8:30 p.m., reconvened at 9:59 p.m. and adjourned at 10:00 p.m. Secretary: Nancy L. Philippart.

**June 8, 2010 workshop (Administrative Center).** Vice President Miletti convened at 6:00 p.m. with Edmunds, Hauff, Philippart and Pochodylo; Fleming and Underwood were absent. Superintendent Fowler and administrators Adamczyk, Davisson, Keeling, Machesky, McAvoy, Papasian and Witt attended with one community member. Topics: public communication, enrollment and staffing update, Principal Financial Resources, transparency report, property/casualty/liability insurance for 2011/2012, and the 2010/2011 budget update. Adjourned 9:42 p.m.

**June 15, 2010 minutes (Services Building).** A public hearing on the preliminary 2010-2011 budget presented by Mr. Adamczyk closed at 7:15 p.m.; the meeting began at 7:16 p.m. with all seven members and approximately 56 audience members. Troy High School received the 2010 Summer Leadership Camp scholarship from the SET SEG Educational Foundation, presented by account executive Thomas Longhway to student council advisor Ryan Werenka. Retirees recognized represented a total of 1,046 years of service. Kathy Hayes of the Michigan Association of School Boards gave Mrs. Carol Pochodylo an Advocacy Award, congratulated Mrs. Nancy Philippart on her second level of board certification, and presented the Board the 2009 Honor Board Award and 2009 Standard of Excellence Award. Resolution 10-060 approved the May 18, 2010 minutes and the May 2010 Treasurer's Report. 10-061 extended the Superintendent's contract from July 1, 2010 through June 30, 2013 without tenure in the administrative position. 10-062 extended the contracts of Richard M. Machesky, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction, and Jasen M. Witt, Assistant Superintendent, Human Resources, through June 30, 2012. 10-063 extended contracts through June 30, 2012 subject to the Administrative Handbook layoff provision for principals including Mark Dziatczak, Lara Dixon and Joseph Hosang, nine assistant principals, directors Scott Bryan, Michael Jolly, Timothy J. McAvoy and Kenneth Miller, supervisors Frank Lams and John Schiesler, Finance Director Monica Papasian and Anne Mull. 10-064 issued a two-year probationary contract to Jeremey Whan as Principal of Bemis Elementary as of July 1, 2010, and 10-065 the same to Mr. Mark Rajter as Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, effective July 1, 2010. 10-066 authorized bidding property/casualty/liability insurance for 2011/2012 and notifying current provider M.A.I.S.L. Budget amendment 10-067 set 2009-10 appropriations at General Fund $138,643,792, Special Revenue Funds 7,682,186, Debt Service Funds 18,461,564, Capital Project Funds 3,288,459 and Internal Service Funds 720,000. Resolution 10-068 set 2010-11 appropriations at General Fund $135,793,505, Special Revenue Funds 5,445,677, Debt Service funds 18,590,065, Capital Project Funds 7,216,120 and Internal Service Funds 120,000, with non-homestead general operating 18.0000 mills, homestead general operating 5.0381 mills, debt retirement on all properties 4.7000 mills and commercial personal property general operating 11.0381 mills. All votes were Yes: 7, No: 0. Dr. Fowler reported that with 24 additional teacher retirements under the state incentive plan plus resignations and full-year leaves, she was confident most if not all teachers notified of layoff in April would be recalled. Adjourned 8:59 p.m.

**Copy paper, bid 9679.** Bids opened June 29, 2010 for white high speed xerographic paper, 8 1/2 x 11, 20#, 92 brightness, 500 sheets per ream, 10 reams per case, total quantity 1,680 cases. Ten bidders were invited and 13 responded, one a No Bid. Midland Paper was low at a unit price of 26.362 for $44,288.16, ahead of RIS Paper 26.57 / 44,637.60; Global Office Solutions 97 brightness 27.25 / 45,780.00 and 92 brightness 27.45 / 46,116.00; Paper Express 27.75 / 46,620.00; Xerox 27.90 / 46,872.00; Office Express 27.95 / 46,956.00; A-1 Business Products 28.50 / 47,880.00; Office Star 30.67 / 51,525.60; Global Associates Computers and Safety Nerds 32.23 / 54,146.40; and Arete Office Supplies 38.00 / 63,840.00. Amerisource submitted No Bid; EIS Solutions, Kerr Albert and One Stop did not respond. Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052, fax 248-823-4077, recommended the award July 1, 2010 to Mark S. Rajter as an expenditure of the 2010/11 General Fund.

**Elementary science kits, bid 9683.** Bids opened July 1, 2010 for kits used at all 12 elementary schools; 13 bidders invited, four responded, three of them No Bids. Lams recommended award July 7, 2010 to Delta Education for $138,280.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. Line items: 12 Animals 2x2 at 525.00 / 6,300.00; 10 Balance and Motion 535.00 / 5,350.00; 10 Earth Materials 675.00 / 6,750.00; 10 Earth Processes 620.00 / 6,200.00; 10 Environments 675.00 / 6,750.00; 10 Insects 675.00 / 6,750.00; 10 Magnetism and Electricity 775.00 / 7,750.00; 10 Measurement 800.00 / 8,000.00; 10 Mixtures and Solutions 740.00 / 7,400.00; 13 New Plants 700.00 / 9,100.00; 10 Newton's Toybox 600.00 / 6,000.00; 13 Pebbles Sand 730.00 / 9,490.00; 13 Solids and Liquids 830.00 / 10,790.00; 10 Structures of Life 650.00 / 6,500.00; 10 Variables 600.00 / 6,000.00; 10 Water 740.00 / 7,400.00; 12 Wood and Paper 800.00 / 9,600.00; 10 You and Your Body 475.00 / 4,750.00; and 10 Air & Weather 740.00 / 7,400.00. Flinn Scientific, Benz Optics Center and Cynmar Corp submitted No Bid; American 3B Scientific, Arbor Scientific, Carolina Biological, Fisher Science Ed., Frey Scientific, Nasco, Pasco Scientific, Sargent Welch and Science Kit LLC did not respond.

**Playground surface materials, bid 9681.** Bids opened July 6, 2010 to replenish playground safety surfacing at all 12 elementary schools; ten bidders invited, one responded. Reviewed with Ken Miller, Director of Operations, and awarded to Rolar Property Services for $74,340.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund: Barnard 5,300.00; Bemis 6,110.00; Costello 7,360.00; Hamilton 6,550.00; Hill 5,300.00; Leonard 5,300.00; Martell 7,140.00; Morse 5,300.00; Schroeder 6,260.00; Troy Union 5,300.00; Wass 7,800.00; Wattles 6,620.00. Non-responders were Brink Wood Products, Interlake Landscaping Service, Kamps Inc., KJP Sales, Landscape Direct, Miracle Recreation of Michigan, Outdoor Fun Store, Saf-Play Services and Sinclair Recreation.

**Radio frequency microphones, bid 9684.** Scott Bryan, Director of Technology at the Technology Resource Center, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248-823-5090, fax 248-823-5050), reported July 7, 2010 that FCC action prohibiting long-used wireless frequencies forces replacement, that requests to federal legislators for waivers or funding failed, and that bid 9684 was released June 21, 2010 with bids opened July 6. Twenty-one valid responses arrived plus one fax response rejected per district policy. Award is recommended to Videotape Products, Inc. of Burbank, California at $24,623.05 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, with replacement done in-house. Quantities bid: 5 Azden 325ULH, 4 Azden 325ULT, 9 Azden BC-29, 5 Sennheiser EW345 G3-B, 6 Sennheiser EW322 G3-B, 2 Sennheiser SK500 G3-B, 2 Sennheiser EM500 G3-B, 18 Sennheiser EW172G3, 6 Sennheiser SKM 100-835-G3, 2 Sennheiser G3OMNIKIT8, 4 Sennheiser ASA1/NT, 4 Sennheiser BB25, 4 Shure A13HD and freight. Other totals: VSC Inc. 19,614.57, Jireh Supplies 19,838.13, Aves A/V Systems 21,154.08, Troxell Communications 26,566.00, B & H Photo 26,838.00, West LA Music 27,105.00, Advanced Lighting & Sound 27,116.50, Washington Music Center 27,330.95, Focus Camera 27,807.00, Perlmutter Purchasing Power 28,258.55, Thalner Electronic Labs 28,359.00, Gridworks Inc. 28,593.59, Aprisa Technology 28,753.38, Audio Visual Innovations / AVI-SPL 29,505.00, NBS-City Animation 29,887.00, Photomart Cine Video 30,302.10, Sound Planning Communications 31,174.81, Sound Engineering 32,504.96 and Business Services 39,160.58; Broadcast Supply Worldwide priced only the Azden items and freight, at 6,884.00.

**Curriculum resolutions.** Item 7.A enrolls the six secondary schools of the district, City of Troy, County of Oakland, as members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association from August 1, 2010 through July 31, 2011, not revocable during that term, adopting the association's constitution, by-laws and handbook rules. Item 7.B adopts a limited Schools of Choice program under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996 for 2010-2011, accepting nonresident applicants from districts in another county whose intermediate school district is contiguous with the Oakland ISD, for anticipated grade 10 seats at the International Academy East; applications July 19 to August 3, 2010.

**MAISL trust and Wattles easement.** Item 8.D names Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, Director and Patricia Orczykowski, Administrative Assistant, Alternate Director to the MAISL Joint Risk Management Trust, the district's property, casualty and liability carrier. Item 8.E is a report by Mark Rajter requiring no action on work with Clark Hill and the City of Troy toward a sidewalk easement at 553 Colebrook for children attending Wattles Elementary School. The draft instrument has Satyendra N. Basu of 553 Colebrook, Troy, Michigan 48083-5110 granting the Troy School District, at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098-4799, a permanent sidewalk easement for consideration of $1.00 over the south 82.00 feet of the west 33 feet of Lot 58 of Cloverdale Farms, recorded in Liber 33, Page 13, Oakland County records, plus the part of the NE 1/4 of Section 22, T2N-R11E lying north of Cloverdale Farms and westerly and southerly of Hidden Ridge Subdivision, Liber 173, Pages 5-7; tax parcel identification part of 88-20-22-252-036. The easement runs with the land, is to be recorded with the Oakland County Register of Deeds, and is exempt from state and county transfer tax under MCL 207.505(a) and 207.526(a). Recording fee $20.00; drafted by Kevin M. Nalu, Esq., Clark Hill PLC, 151 South Old Woodward Avenue, Suite 200, Birmingham, Michigan 48009.

**Treasurer, depositories and investments.** Item 10.A appoints Mark S. Rajter Treasurer of the Troy Board of Education for July through December 2010. Item 10.B adopts the fund depositories and investment resolution for the same period, directing the Treasurer to deposit all public monies including tax monies with Bank of America, Bank of New York, Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, MILAF and PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank. Withdrawals may be made by facsimile signature of Treasurer Rajter and, in emergencies, by his handwritten signature or that of Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, who may sign on the General Fund and Payroll accounts at Bank of America. Troy Career Center accounts at PNC Bank require the handwritten signature of Robert Stromayer, Dorothy Kaltz, Jennifer Llewellyn or Kathy Molesa. The Bank of America account for health care and dependent care claims uses the Treasurer's facsimile signature, with checks over $10,000 also requiring the handwritten signature of Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources, or Monica Papasian, Finance Director. Funds may be invested under Board Policy D-1103, and the Treasurer may combine money from more than one fund under subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code, with authorized institutions Ambassador Capital Management, Bank of America, Chase Bank, Charter One Bank, Citizens Bank, Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, First Empire Securities, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF, Morgan Stanley Smith Barney, PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank and The Private Bank. Certified the 13th day of July 2010.

**Summer tax, workshop and closed session.** Item 10.C continues summer tax collections for the 2011-2012 fiscal year with notice to the City of Troy. The annual summer tax resolution recites that by resolution of July 13, 2010 the Board determined to impose a summer property tax levy collecting one-half of school property taxes including debt service beginning with 2011 and continuing until specifically revoked; it invokes for 2010 the previously adopted ongoing resolution under 1976 P.A. 451 as amended, directs that requests reach each city's governing body before January 1, 2011, and authorizes negotiation of collection expenses billable under MCLA 380.1612 subject to Board approval, with certification under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, P.A. 1976. Item 10.D schedules a Special Board Workshop on the facilities review process for Tuesday, August 17, 2010 at 5:30 p.m. at the Administrative Center. Item 11.A calls a closed session on negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(c) by roll call of Philippart, Pochodylo, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff and Miletti, after which only adjournment follows.
